## 0 · The year in one paragraph

🔗 **New to this client? Read §0A first** — it explains the company, every document and what each
one is for, from zero.

A single-shareholder Florida S corporation running general freight trucking, **no W-2 payroll in
2025** ⚠️ *(2024 paid the officer 25,000 — §4 decision 1 is open)*, no QuickBooks and no bookkeeper —
the books arrive once a year as the firm's own spreadsheet template, filled in by the client. 2025 revenue is up about 23% on 2024 while the
client's own profit line collapses to near nothing, and **the collapse is at least partly an
artifact**: one expense line's own label says it includes loan principal. ⚠️ **How much of the fall it
explains is not established** — depreciation also dropped and a home-office allocation was newly
booked. The year also carries six equipment additions, four disposals — 🆕 **a fifth was ruled on
2026-09-25** *(decision 33)* — including **a truck destroyed and settled by insurance**, personal cars moving through the
business account, and a home-office allocation computed the way a sole proprietor would.

It owns tractors and trailers and hauls other people's goods. ⚠️ **How it is PAID is not established** — §3E ⑤ found the two largest payers arriving under **payroll-style ACH captions**, and records that *"customer"* is the natural reading, **not a quotation** |

### ③ The documents — what each one IS, and what a tax preparer does with it

**Grouped by the job it does, not by who sent it.** ⚠️ *Where a row states a general accounting or
legal proposition it is stated from knowledge, not read off a form — the same marking §3C, §3D and
§3F carry.*

| Document | What it physically is | What it is FOR on the return |
|---|---|---|
| **The tax organizer** | A questionnaire in Double the client answers online | The **yes/no facts** — states, employees, 1099s, accounting method. ⚠️ **Its silence is not evidence**: it is conditional, so a wrong answer hides the follow-up questions. ⓘ *This client's is **75% complete and never submitted** (§1 row 4)* |
| **The books** *(`Balance Sheet & P&L Templates.xlsx`)* | The firm's spreadsheet, filled in by the client | **The income statement** — ⓘ *and more: the same workbook carries the **2025 asset list** (§3C), an **older 2023 asset list** (all of §3G) and the broken balance-sheet tab* |
| **The home-office worksheet** | A separate spreadsheet the client fills in | **The allocation behind the home-office figure** *(§3D)* — one of the three positions Julia must settle |
| **Bank statements** *(twelve monthly PDFs)* | The checking account, month by month | ⚠️ **NOT the income statement.** They give the **cash balance** at each year end, and they are **the main window** on what the owner took out. ⛔ **Not the only one and not a complete one:** §3E ④ says **not one counterparty is ESTABLISHED as owner-facing**, §3E ⑥ says a bare wire or a check *"matches no string and is invisible to this method"*, and §3J makes the card summary a second window |
| **Credit-card year-end summary** | The issuer's annual recap, itemised by category and merchant | **What the card BOUGHT** — so business spending can be separated from personal. ⛔ **It does NOT give a balance**, which is what Schedule L needs *(§3J ⓪)* |
| 🔑 **Interest letter / *"tax breakout letter"*** | A one-page January letter from a lender | **THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD DOCUMENT HERE.** A truck payment is **part interest, part principal**. **Interest is deductible; principal is NOT** — it repays a debt, and the truck is deducted separately through depreciation. **This letter splits them, and states the loan balance at 31 December.** ⚠️ **Not the only route** — §3H ② names the contracts' own amortization schedules. ✅ 🆕 **CORRECTED 2026-09-15 — BOTH CLAIMS THIS CELL USED TO MAKE WERE INVERTED.** ✅ **The three 2025 letters we hold ARE BMO's, all three** *(§4 decision 21 — Lilian opened them)*. ✅ **The two AP Equipment notes need no letter: they are COMPUTED from the notes themselves** *(§3U ⑨)*. ✅ **The Audi is a LEASE — no principal, no interest, no letter, ever** *(§3U ⑥)*. 🔴 **Still open: IPFS only.** ⛔ 🆕 **CORRECTED 2026-09-27 — three of the four this cell listed are CLOSED and the fourth was never needed: Mitsubishi by its own year-end email (decision 26), the Fifth Third line of credit by its December statement (decision 31), the SBA by its own statements (decision 23), and Financial Pacific by the caption search in our own statements (§3AD ②, decision 50).** ⛔ **Ask none of them for anything.** _(As written: Still open: IPFS, Mitsubishi, the Fifth Third line of credit, the SBA, and a Financial Pacific balance letter.)_ *(§3U ⑪ — the canonical list)*. ⛔ **AND FINANCIAL PACIFIC IS NO LONGER "the exception and the model": §3U ⑤ finds nine payments where its schedule assumes twelve, so its 3,198.13 and 18,837.47 may NOT be keyed until a balance letter arrives.** _(As written:)_ ⛔ **Only three 2025 ones exist here** — none for BMO ×3, both AP Equipment notes, the Audi lease, IPFS, the credit line or the SBA. ✅ **Financial Pacific is the exception and the model:** its own 2024 letters plus its amortization schedule settle both its contracts *(§3H ③ter, ③ter-bis)* |
| 🔑 **Secured promissory note / finance contract** | The loan agreement signed at purchase | **Proves the terms** — amount financed, rate, number of payments — and **the VIN of the exact vehicle**. ⚠️ **It proves the date of the NOTE, not of the purchase:** §3H ③bis records that *"a truck bought in 2023 and **refinanced** in 2025 produces exactly this document"* |
| 🔑 **Retail purchase agreement / dealer invoice** | The sales document from the truck dealer | **Proves what the asset COST and when it was PLACED IN SERVICE** — the two inputs depreciation is built from. ⚠️ **A loan amount is NOT a cost**: cash or a trade-in may have gone to the dealer on top |
| 🔑 **Sale agreement** *(for something sold)* | The sales document, the other way round | **Proves the PROCEEDS.** Gain or loss = proceeds − *(cost − depreciation already taken)*. ⛔ **No document, no COMPUTABLE gain — the disposal is still reportable**, and §6 keeps Form 4797 open regardless |
| 🔑 **Insurance settlement letter** *(for something destroyed)* | The insurer's letter stating what it paid | **The proceeds figure for a total loss** — the sale agreement's equivalent when there is no buyer *(§4 decision 9)* |
| **The prior-year filed return** | Last year's finished 1120-S | 🔑 **The answer key.** The **opening balance sheet**, the **depreciation schedule every asset continues on**, and **the firm's own conventions** |

### ④ Why the truck documents matter more here than anywhere else

**A truck is not an expense. It is an asset**, deducted a piece at a time over several years
*(depreciation)*. To do that the return needs, **for every single vehicle**: what it cost · **when it
was placed in service** · how much has been deducted so far · and, when it leaves, what it sold for.

🔴 **And on this client none of that can be matched by NAME.** §3G ① establishes **two** naming
systems the client uses *(a description list and a unit-number list)* and **a third on the returns**
*(`#7107` / `#1800` / `HU4577`)*. ✅ 🆕 **ANSWERED 2026-09-25 — §3AC ④: `1838` is the `2022 Frght Cascadia`, asset #7 on the 2024 return, and §6's row for it is TICKED.** _(As written:)_ ⚠️ **A possible fourth — `1838` on an interest letter — is flagged
by §3H ① as *"a fourth naming system, OR A TYPO. Ask,"* and is still open in §6.**

🔑 **The finance documents supply the VIN, which is why §3H ③ says the mapping should be asked for
against VINs rather than descriptions.** ⛔ **But a VIN is not a key all parties share — §3I ⑦
establishes that NEITHER FILED RETURN CARRIES ONE.** *(An earlier draft said it was; withdrawn.)*

### ⑤ What 2024 did — a POINTER TABLE, not a set of instructions

🛑 **Read the header rule above before this table. "What 2024 did" is NOT the same as "what 2025
should do"** — and for three of these rows the section it points at says the opposite.

| | What 2024 did | Does it carry to 2025? |
|---|---|---|
| The expense base | Almost everything to **page 1 line 20** with an itemised statement, not the named lines *(§3A, §3A-bis)* | ✅ **Yes — §4 decision 4** |
| Meals | **Half added back** on Schedule M-1 *(§3A-bis)* | ⚠️ **Decision 6, and it is CLAUDE's, not Julia's** — and §3A-bis ④-bis carries a live objection: **entertainment is disallowed in full, not half**, and DOT meals sit at a different rate. **Ask before repeating it on a year 3.4× larger** |
| The home office | 🔴 **EXCLUDED ENTIRELY**, proved by two exact checks *(§3A-bis ②)* | 🔴 **Julia's — decision 2** |
| New equipment | **§179 elected at ZERO**, and an **election OUT of bonus depreciation** attached *(§3A, §3A-bis ④)* | 🔴 **Decision 3 is open** · ☑️ **the election-out must be RE-ATTACHED — it is annual** |
| The owner's money | **K-1 113,157 · M-2 line 7 51,988 · paid-in capital (61,169)**, and `113,157 − 51,988 = 61,169` exactly *(§3I ③)* | ⛔ **NO.** §3A forbids stating **the mechanism** as what the preparer did — *"the identity is exact; the mechanism is inferred."* 🛑 **And §3I ③ calls the 2024 presentation a candidate DEFECT to put to the signer, not a house method** — while **§5C-v gate 4 FAILS, so 2025 is prepared GROSS** |
| Cash on the balance sheet | **One bank account** *(§3I ②)* | ✅ **YES — but by RULING, not by analogy.** §3I ② is titled *"why it is NOT yet a convention to copy"* and its objection stands: **copying a presentation cannot cure an ownership question.** 🔑 **Lilian OVERRODE it on 2026-09-14** — *only the accounts the 2024 return reported are the company's* — so cash is **5,788.50 unconditionally** *(§3K, §4 decision 11)*. ⚠️ **The objection travels to Julia WITH the decision** *(§3K ⑤, decision 11a)* |
| The debt | **One aggregate number**, no breakdown *(§3I ④)* | ⚠️ **Only the PRESENTATION.** §3I ④: *"what the analogy saves is a Schedule L statement, not the collection work"* |
| Disposals | **No capitalised asset left the 2024 schedule** — gross depreciable assets rose by exactly the two additions *(§3I ⑥)* | ⛔ **Nothing to copy — but state it as §3I ⑥ does.** *"No 4797 was ever filed"* is **NOT established** *(pages 15 and 18 produce no text)*, *"2023 disposed of nothing"* needs **the 2022 schedule nobody has read**, and **an uncapitalised disposal is invisible to this check while still needing a 4797** |

🔑 **That last row is still why §4 decision 9 had to come from Julia rather than from the prior
year** — there is **no VISIBLE prior-year method** for a disposal.

### 🔑 3A-bis · THE ANALOGY TABLE — what 2024 DID with each line, and what 2025 does with it

🔴 **This is the most valuable thing in this paper, and it comes from ONE page of the filed return**
that the first pass never opened: **page 16, the `Line 20 (1120S) — Other Deductions` statement**,
itemised caption by caption. With it, every book line maps to what the return actually did.

> ⚠️ **Four of the sixteen captions came through the extraction as `[GLYPH]`** — their values are
> unreadable. **They are recovered by arithmetic, not by reading**, and the arithmetic is exact: see
> the reconciliation below.

#### ① The reconciliation — books → return, and it ties to the dollar

**Source of the 2024 book figures below: the client's own `Income Statement (2024)` sheet** in the
same workbook *(§1 source 1)* — **not** the return. The 19 lines on that sheet total 973,895.08 to the
cent. ⚠️ **The 2024 return was re-opened on 2026-09-13 to read page 16**, after the first pass's
redacted text had been deleted.

```
2024 book expenses (19 lines)                            973,895.08
  less Interest            (own line, page 1 line 13)    -12,110.08
  less Depreciation        (books; return uses 4562)     -54,000.00
  = base carried to the line 20 statement                907,785.00
  less meals disallowed    (50% — M-1 add-back)           -5,909.00
  🔴 less Office lease/house,utility                      -7,951.00
  = 893,925  ←  EXACTLY the return's line 20              ✅
```

#### ①-bis 🔑 THE INDEPENDENT CHECK — and it is the one that earns the conclusion

⚠️ **The reconciliation above proves only that the 7,951 is not inside LINE 20.** It says nothing
about lines 9–12 or 16–19, and ⛔ **reading those as blank is exactly what §1 forbids.** The check
that closes them uses two operands neither reconciliation touches:

```
gross receipts                 1,044,320
 − officer compensation           25,000   (page 1 line 7)
 − interest                       12,110   (page 1 line 13)
 − depreciation                   35,861   (page 1 line 14)
 − other deductions              893,925   (page 1 line 20)
 = 77,424  =  page 1 line 22, exactly           ✅
```

🔑 **Page 1 closes to the dollar with no room for another deduction line.** Had the 7,951 been taken
anywhere on page 1, line 22 would read **69,473**. **That — not a blank cell — is what establishes
that it was not deducted.**

🔑 **And a third, free corroboration, from the M-1:** the client's own 2024 book income is
`1,044,320 − 973,895.08 − 25,000` = **45,424.92**, while Schedule M-1 line 1 as filed is **71,515** —
a gap of **26,090.08**, against the depreciation difference *(54,000 − 35,861 = 18,139)*
**plus the home office (7,951) = 26,090** — ⚠️ **a residual of 8 cents, which is the interest
rounding** *(the books carry 12,110.08, the return 12,110)*. **Not exact, and close enough to be
evidence rather than coincidence.** ✅ **So 2024's M-1 line 1 was built from a TAX-ADJUSTED book column,
not from the client's books**, and it carries neither reconciling item on its face.
🔑 **That also answers §3A's open flag** about the missing depreciation add-back: the adjustment was
made **before** the M-1, inside the book-income figure, rather than on it.

**And the four unreadable captions — their TOTAL is pinned, their individual values are not:** the twelve readable captions sum to
**847,972** *(⚠️ with meals at the NET 5,908, not the gross 11,817 — re-adding the table's own column
gives 853,881)*, the statement totals **893,925**, so the masked rows carry **45,953** — and the four
book lines not yet accounted for *(Agents/Crossdock 19,800 · IFTA/HUT/Permits 10,058 · Heavy haul
equipment 12,100 · TRT Wash 3,995)* sum to **45,953 exactly**.

✅ **What that DOES establish, and it is enough:** no subset of those four plus 7,951 also sums to
45,953, so **the home office cannot be hiding inside the masked group.** That question is closed.
⛔ **What it does NOT establish is which masked row holds which value** — any four numbers totalling
45,953 satisfy the arithmetic. **Three of the four are matched to their book lines because the
caption NAMES were readable**, which is a reading, not arithmetic.
⚠️ **And ①-bis, not this, is the independent confirmation** — ① and ② are algebraically the same
equation stated twice.

#### ② 🔴 THE HOME OFFICE — the answer, and it is not what the books do

🔑 🆕 **FIRST, BECAUSE LILIAN ASKED THE RIGHT QUESTION ON 2026-09-27 — *"si fue excluido, ¿cómo sabes
entonces que fueron 7,951?"* — THE TWO FACTS COME FROM TWO DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS, and that is the whole
answer:**

| The fact | Which document | How it says so |
|---|---|---|
| **The AMOUNT was 7,951** | 🔑 **the CLIENT's own 2024 Profit & Loss** — his book line `Office lease/house,utility` | **He wrote it. It is his bookkeeping, not the return** |
| **It was EXCLUDED** | 🔑 **the FILED 2024 RETURN** | **Page 1 closes to the dollar WITHOUT it: 1,044,320 − 25,000 − 12,110 − 35,861 − 893,925 = 77,424, exactly line 22.** ⛔ **Had the 7,951 been deducted, line 22 would read 69,473** |

✅ **So nothing is being read off a return that does not carry it.** **His books say he spent it; the return
says the firm did not deduct it; and the arithmetic is what makes "did not deduct it" a measurement rather
than an impression.** ⚠️ **What the return CANNOT say is where the 7,951 was debited instead** — it fell out
of the expense base before the M-1, **so a distribution, a receivable from the shareholder and officer
compensation all look identical from the outside.** _(The rest of this subsection is as written.)_

**2024 did NOT deduct it.** The book line `Office lease/house,utility` — **7,951** — **is not in the
line 20 statement** *(reconciliation ①, exact)* **and was not taken on any other page-1 deduction
line** *(check ①-bis: page 1 closes to the dollar without it; with it, line 22 would be 69,473)*.
⚠️ **Page 1 line 11, Rents, also reads blank in the extracted text** — that is consistent with the
above but is **not** the evidence, since §1 bars reading an absence off this extraction.
**It was removed from the expense base**, and both checks are exact only because it was.

| | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Book line `Office lease/house,utility` | **7,951** | **27,248** — **3.4× higher** |
| Separate home-office worksheet from the client | **none found** — no 2024 organizer or worksheet is in §1's source list, and none was searched for | **yes** — `Home Office Deduction … .xlsx`, ⅓ of the whole home |
| **What the return did with it** | 🔴 **EXCLUDED — not deducted** | **The analogy says: exclude it** |

🔑 **So the analogy answer is: take the 27,248 out of the expense base, exactly as 2024 took the
7,951 out.**

🔴 **BUT "exclude it" IS ONLY HALF AN ANSWER, AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT IN THIS PAPER YET.** The
company actually paid that money; a debit that stops being an expense has to land somewhere —

#### ④ Depreciation — the convention is explicit, and it is an ELECTION with a statement

**Page 20 of the 2024 return is an `Elections` page:**

> *"Pursuant to IRC Section 168(k)(2)(D)(iii), the Taxpayer elects out of first-year special
> depreciation for all **3-Year** depreciable property placed in service during the current tax
> year."* — **and the same election for 5-Year property.**

🔑 **So there was no bonus because the firm ELECTED OUT, deliberately, with an attached statement.**
⚠️ **The election out of bonus is made annually, by property class, on a timely filed return — so if
2025 repeats it the statement must be attached again, and if it is not attached bonus applies by
default.** ⛔ **Stated from knowledge and NOT read off the 2025 instructions or the Code — verify
before relying on it**, and note the quoted cite is the software's pre-TCJA wording. **The 2025 bonus
rate also has to be looked up**, because "bonus applies by default" is a different number this year.
**This is the kind of attachment that blocks e-file when it is missing** *(delivery rule 6)*.

🛑 **And rule 6 says DRAFT it, so here it is — English, plain ASCII, ready to paste**, with the
classes left to be confirmed against 2025's own additions *(2024's statement named 3-year and 5-year
only, which was enough because all eight assets were 5-year)*:

ELECTION OUT OF FIRST-YEAR SPECIAL DEPRECIATION ALLOWANCE

Pursuant to IRC Section 168(k)(7), the Taxpayer elects out of the additional
first-year depreciation deduction for all classes of property placed in

**The workbook has an OLDER `Asset List` sheet** *(the 2023 one, carried forward inside the same
file)* that nobody had opened until late on 2026-09-13. It **narrows** §3F's mapping problem and
raises three other questions.

⛔ **It does NOT unblock Form 4797.** What it maps is the client's **description** list to the tax
schedule. **His UNIT NUMBERS — 1834, 1835, 1836, which is how his DISPOSAL table names the trucks —
are still unmapped**, and that is the map Form 4797 needs. **§3F's ask stands unchanged.**

### ① The description list lines up with the tax schedule by DATE and COST — approximately

| The client's description | Tax schedule | Date gap | Cost gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 Freightliner Cascadia, in service **2021-06-01**, purchase **78,000** | **#7107**, 6/16/2021, **78,145** | 15 days | 145 |
| 2018 Freightliner Cascadia, in service **2021-08-01**, purchase **100,000** | **#1800**, 7/20/2021, **100,245** | 12 days, **crosses the month** | 245 |
| 2018 FRGHT Cascadia, in service **2020-05-01**, *"paid off"* | **HU4577**, 5/15/2020, **46,000** | 14 days | ⛔ **no cost given at all** |
| 2015 Utility Trailer, *"paid off"* | **not on the schedule at all** | — | ⚠️ fully depreciated, or never capitalised |

⚠️ **Not one row matches exactly on either axis, so these are CONSISTENT WITH, not CONFIRMED** — and
the third row has only an approximate date behind it. **This file applies the stricter standard forty
lines earlier**: §3F flags a 3,299 cost gap as a discrepancy and marks these same rows `~`. **A
plausible reading — the client's dates are month-rounded and his costs are invoice price against a
capitalised cost including tax and fees — is an EXPLANATION, not a verification.** ⛔ **The

names **`2018 FRGHT unit 1835`** and **`unit 1836`**. **So he has two naming systems** *(a description
list and a unit-number list)* **and the return has a third** *(#7107 / #1800 / HU4577)*.

🔴 **AND THE POSSIBLE CONSEQUENCE IS LARGE — as a question, not a finding.** The client's 2025 sheet
disposes of units **1834, 1835 and 1836** — **three 2018 Freightliners** — and the 2024 tax schedule
carries **exactly three** 2018 Freightliners, cost **224,390** between them *(78,145 + 100,245 +

**1835** and **1836**; **1834 is known only from the client's own disposal-table label** — his third
naming system.

only the 410,452 aggregate *(§7)*. **No claim is made about how big it is.**

### ③ 🛑 AND HERE IS WHAT TRAVELS WITH IT — the ruling does NOT make anything disappear

**🔴 (a) Payments to a card that is not the company's are NOT COMPANY EXPENSES — and this file does
NOT establish what they are instead.** If the Fifth Third credit card and the Macy's card are not the
company's accounts, then **every payment the business bank account made to them in 2025 was the
company discharging a liability that was never its own.**
🔑 **§3A-bis ② already wrote the rule that governs this, in another context:** *"a debit that stops
being an expense has to land somewhere — a **distribution**, a **receivable from the shareholder**,
or **officer compensation**. ⛔ Nothing establishes which."* **Nothing in this file evidences a
receivable or wages** — ⛔ **but "nothing evidences the other two" is not "it is the first."**
§3A-bis ② never resolved it, and §3K ① observes only that *the prior year offers no precedent* for a
receivable, which is an absence in a different year, not evidence about 2025. 🔑 **The choice is
open, it is JULIA's, and the three land in three different places on three different returns** — a
**distribution** reduces equity and goes to the shareholder's §1368 analysis; a **receivable** is a
Schedule L asset and nothing else; **officer compensation** is a page-1 deduction that carries
payroll tax and a W-2.
⛔ **An earlier draft went further and said a distribution here "is taxable to the shareholder" while
the other two "are not." Both halves are wrong and it is withdrawn.** Under **§1368(b)(2)** — which
applies because there is no accumulated E&P *(§8)* — what makes a distribution taxable is the
shareholder's **STOCK BASIS**, not the AAA, and 🛑 **his basis is an open item this file does not
hold** *(§6 — his prior-year Form 7203 line 15, filed with his 1040)*. **And officer compensation is
ordinary income to him plus payroll tax** — not taxable *under §1368*, which is not the same thing as
not taxable.
⛔ **An earlier draft headed this *"are DISTRIBUTIONS"* while the body said the opposite — the same
failure §3J ④'s own preamble withdrew on itself *("it points at the second Amex")*. A heading is what
survives skimming. Withdrawn.**

**🔴 (b) The same applies to the property tax, conditionally.** The company sent **14,140.18** to the
county *(§3E ④)*. **If that is the shareholder's home property tax, it is the same act as paying his
credit card** — a personal obligation discharged from the company's account, which does not become a
company expense by being paid from there. ⛔ **The condition is NOT closed** — §3G ② keeps the
commercial-vehicle-registration reading live.

**🔴 (c) The "sweep" reading of the four other Fifth Third accounts DIES.** §3E ③ concluded the four
were *"a pass-through / sweep — neither income nor expense."* 🛑 **A sweep is movement between a
company's OWN accounts. The ruling removes that premise.** **53 lines and 47,884.46 went OUT to an
outside party; 17 lines and 51,231.00 came IN — and they can no longer be netted.** ⚠️ *The ruling
establishes the accounts are not the company's; it does not establish whose they are.*

**🔴 (d) §3E ⑥'s bounded range "≈ 0 to ≈ 137,927" is WITHDRAWN, and it cannot be rebuilt from this
file.** Its floor of ≈ 0 required the transfers to net to nothing and the Amex and Broward to be
fully business. **Under the ruling the transfers alone contribute 47,884.46 gross, and two new rows
enter it — the 2025 payments to the Fifth Third card and to Macy's.** 🛑 **NEITHER OF THOSE TWO HAS A

### ⑤ ⓘ THE MOST LIKELY METHOD — marked as INFERENCE, and it is the same method Lilian just described · ⛔ 🆕 **BUT §4 DECISION 22 BARS IT FOR 2025** *(§3U ④: 76% of the 2025 outflows is one block that turns out to be driver payments, so a residual would sweep most of a million dollars into the capital account)*. **This section describes what the PRIOR preparer most likely did; it is not what this return will do.**

ⓘ *Stated from reasoning, not read off any document.* **A preparer with no books derives the
distribution as a RESIDUAL** — total cash out, less the uses that are identified as the company's
(deductible expenses, loan principal, asset purchases). What is left went to the owner.

same way, **the ruling of §3K makes it BIGGER, not smaller** — every payment to a non-company card
and every transfer to a non-company account is now an unidentified use of company cash, which is
exactly what a residual sweeps up *(§3K ③)*.

_(🆕 **2026-09-15, and it needed NOTHING from the client.** Lilian asked why the firm was requesting
bank statements it already had. **It was right to ask — they were on file and readable.** The twelve
Fifth Third statements were **re-read from Double through [`tools/redact-doc/`](../../../tools/redact-doc/)**,

§3R ③ and §3S ④ is superseded by this.**)_

### ① ✅ FIRST, THE STRING-MATCH CAVEAT IS RESOLVED — the 39 are real and they total exactly

§3E ② warned that **123,786.73 was a STRING MATCH** — *"39 lines whose description contained `AMEX`,
not 39 payments somebody identified"* — and §3S ④ carried that as the floor's weakest input.
✅ **Re-read today: 39 lines, every one captioned `AMEX EPAYMENT ER AM ACH PMT`, summing to
123,786.73 to the cent.** ⛔ **The caveat is discharged, not merely repeated.**

### ② 🔑 THE MATCHING RULE, and it is the document's own behaviour rather than an assumption

**A card payment is initiated at Amex and pulled from the bank afterwards**, so the card's posting
date comes **first** and the bank's debit follows. ✅ **Nineteen pairs match on amount with a lag of
+1 to +4 days, and every single one falls in that window** — **+1 day on thirteen of them**. 🔑 **A
pattern that tight across nineteen independent pairs is the rule being right, not a coincidence
being fitted.**

|---|---|---|

| 🔴 **UNEXPLAINED** — left the bank as `AMEX EPAYMENT`, **never reached this card** | **18 debits** | 🔴 **46,344.31** |
| ⏳ **IN TRANSIT** — after the 12/19 close, so they SHOULD post in the 01/19/26 cycle *(12/23 · 12/29)* | **2 debits** | **5,761.87** |

says — move one debit from MATCHED to UNEXPLAINED and the identity is untouched. ⛔ **An earlier
version of this paragraph called it *"the check every earlier attempt claimed and none of them had"*,
which is precisely the error §3S ① was written to purge, reintroduced one section later.**

|---|---|---|

### ⑦ ℹ️ WHAT AN "SBA EIDL" IS — because Lilian asked and the paper never said

**SBA = the U.S. Small Business Administration. EIDL = Economic Injury Disaster Loan.** It is a
**federal loan**, made directly by the SBA — not by a bank — to businesses hit by a declared disaster.
**Almost every EIDL on a 2020-vintage balance sheet is a COVID one**: 30-year term, **3.75%** for a
business, no collateral under 25,000, and repayment deferred for the first years — which is why the
payments are small and why the balance barely moves.

**Here:** six payments in 2025, **1,272.00** — 159.00 recurring plus one 477.00.
✅ 🆕 **ANSWERED 2026-09-15 — §3V ②: the payments are 100% interest and 0% principal, so the balance is held **while the deferred-interest BACKLOG lasts — a condition that can END** *(§3V ②; an EIDL is not an interest-only product)*. Nothing is asked of the client, and the 2024 presentation was correct.** _(As written:)_ 🔴 **And the prior year is what makes it a question: the 2024 return reported 32,500 in BOTH
columns** — the same balance at the start and the end of a year in which payments were made.
**§3I ④ calls that a likely prior-year defect.** ☑️ **What we need is one number: the principal
balance at 12/31/2025** — and the SBA publishes it in the borrower's own portal, so the client can read
it off a screen rather than request a letter.

### ⑧ ℹ️ WHAT "IPFS" IS — and which insurance

**IPFS is a premium finance company.** The mechanism, because it is not obvious: a commercial trucking
policy is billed as one large annual premium. **IPFS pays the insurer the whole premium up front, and

## 3AD · ✅ THE THREE FREE IN-HOUSE SEARCHES, RUN 2026-09-27 — two of them REVERSE the paper's own finding, and the method is why

> **Lilian, 2026-09-27: *"haz las tres búsquedas gratis en los statements"*.** All twelve 2025 statements
> were re-fetched and re-read through [`tools/redact-doc/`](../../../tools/redact-doc/); **every extract was
> deleted in the same pass.** ⛔ **Nothing was asked of the client.**

### ① 🛑 THE METHOD FAILED, AND IT FAILED THE SAME WAY TWICE — read this before the findings

**Both open items rested on a search BY EXACT AMOUNT.** §3U ② grouped every 2025 debit by its value and
traced each recurring value to its months. ⛔ **That is blind to a lender who varies the draft** — a
documentation fee on the first payment, interim interest between funding and the first due date, a late
charge, a sales-tax adjustment. **The payment is there; the amount is not the one being searched for.**

🔑 **THE RELIABLE KEY IS THE CAPTION, NOT THE AMOUNT.** Every lender pays under its own fixed caption
all year, and the caption does not move when the amount does. ✅ **Both searches were re-run on the
caption, and both reversed.**

⚠️ **This is [`method.md`](../../pre-return-review/method.md) rule 1b in a new place:** a negative belongs
to the search that produced it, and *"nine payments, not twelve"* was a fact about an amount query, not
about the bank account.

## 3AO · 🔴 HOW EACH ASSET IS CLASSIFIED — read off IRS Pub. 946 (2025), and it does NOT agree with the prior year

> **Lilian, 2026-09-27:** *"sé que necesito distinguir si la depreciación es a 3 años o a 5 años, el tipo de
> assets, todo eso tengo que definirlo en ATX. Necesito que leas las reglas y las instrucciones de la IRS y los
> datos del vehículo, y me ayudes a determinar cómo hacer esta clasificación."*

🔑 **Nobody in this firm's sessions had ever checked the class. The prior year's 5-year life was transcribed,
not derived — and it is wrong for the tractors.**

### ① ✅ THE SOURCE, QUOTED — Pub. 946 (2025 edition), Appendix B, Table B-1

📄 **Read 2026-09-27 from `irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf`, the 2025 edition** *(`publication-946/2025`, page
proof dated 13-Mar-2026)*. 🛑 **Not from memory — the skill's own rule.**

| Asset class | What Table B-1 calls it | Class life | 🔑 **GDS recovery period** | ADS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **00.22** | `Automobiles, Taxis` | 3 | **5 years** | 5 |
| **00.241** | `Light General Purpose Trucks` — *"Includes trucks for use over the road (actual weight less than 13,000 pounds)"* | 4 | **5 years** | 5 |
| **00.242** | `Heavy General Purpose Trucks` — *"Includes heavy general purpose trucks, concrete ready mix-trucks, and ore trucks, for use over the road (actual unloaded weight 13,000 pounds or more)"* | 6 | **5 years** | 6 |
| 🔴 **00.26** | `Tractor Units for Use Over-the-Road` | 4 | 🔴 **3 YEARS** | 4 |
| **00.27** | `Trailers and Trailer-Mounted Containers` | 6 | **5 years** | 6 |

🛑 **THE WHOLE POINT IS THE LINE BETWEEN 00.26 AND 00.242.** ✅ **A TRACTOR UNIT — the thing with a fifth
wheel that pulls a semi-trailer and carries no cargo itself — is THREE-YEAR property.** ⛔ **A straight
truck, however heavy, is FIVE-year.** ⚠️ **The distinction is the VEHICLE'S CONFIGURATION, not its weight and
not its brand.**

### ② 🔴 WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS FLEET

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FRT'18 (HU4577)` · `2018 FREIGHTLINER #7107` · `#1800` | **Freightliner tractors** ⚠️ **pending body-type confirmation (③)** | 🔴 **00.26** | 🔴 **3 years** | ⛔ **5 years** |
| `2022 Frght Cascadia (1838)` | **Freightliner tractor** ⚠️ **pending body-type confirmation (③)** — 🔑 **the ONLY tractor that survives to 12/31/2025, and it has ONE filed return** *(⑤)* | 🔴 **00.26** | 🔴 **3 years** | ⛔ **5 years** |
| `2019 Wabash Trailer` · `2023 Utility Trailer` · `2025 Benson` | **Semi-trailers** | ✅ **00.27** | ✅ **5 years** | ✅ **5 years — CORRECT** |
| `AUDI` *(the 2021 car)* | **Automobile** | ✅ **00.22** | ✅ **5 years** | ✅ **5 years — but see ④** |
| 🆕 `1839` · `1837` · `1840` · `146` *(2025 additions)* | **Freightliner Cascadia tractors** ⚠️ **pending body-type confirmation (③) — the model name does NOT establish it** | 🔴 **00.26** | 🔴 **3 years** | — |

📄 **Pub. 946 (2025), verbatim:** *"A passenger automobile is any four-wheeled vehicle made primarily for use

| | |

| **The Audi Q6 e-tron** | ✅ **LEASED, so no depreciation at all.** ⚠️ **What COULD apply is the lessee's §280F(c) INCLUSION AMOUNT — but only if it is a passenger automobile, i.e. GVW ≤ 6,000 lb.** 🔑 **The door-jamb sticker answers it in five seconds, and an electric mid-size SUV is usually ABOVE it, which would mean no inclusion amount at all** |

Its reimbursement line takes the insurance
received FOR THAT PROPERTY — nothing else.** ⇒ ⛔ **A payment reimbursing a TOWING BILL is not proceeds for
the truck.** ✅ **It is a recovery of an expense: it either offsets the towing deduction or is income.**

⇒ ☑️ **SO IN THE ASSET DISPOSITION, ONLY THE VEHICLE'S SHARE IS ENTERED.** 🔑 **On his own words that is
about 20,000, not 57,500** — and **the paper has been carrying 57,500 as the proceeds since §3C and decision 18** ⚠️ *(an earlier version cited §3U, which is the LENDER CENSUS and carries no casualty figure)*. ⛔ **That
would overstate the casualty gain by the towing share.**

⚠️ **AND THE TWO SIDES MUST BE TREATED CONSISTENTLY OR THE RETURN DOUBLE-COUNTS:** **if the ~34,000 towing
was deducted (§3AQ ② — it may be inside his `Auto Repars & Maintenance` of 54,032), its reimbursement is
income. If it was never deducted, its reimbursement is not income either.** ⛔ **One side without the other
is wrong in whichever direction it is taken.**

RUN, AND THE PAPER MUST NOT BE READ AS SAYING IT WAS.** 🔑 **§3E ⑥ is explicit about the limit of its own
credit list: it is *"every movement matching the counterparty strings that were searched"* — NOT every
movement.** **The strings searched were lender and payroll captions. No insurance caption was among them.**

☑️ **WHAT TO LOOK FOR, and the shapes are different enough to distinguish:**

| If the credit looks like… | Then |
|---|---|
| **one credit of ≈57,500** | **the insurer settled everything in one payment** ⇒ **the split is his to allocate, and it is one question** |
| **≈20,000 and ≈34,000 separately** | 🔑 **THE BANK ITSELF SPLITS IT AND NO QUESTION IS NEEDED** — **the best possible outcome** |
| **≈20,000 only** | **the towing was paid direct to the tow company** ⇒ **the 34,000 never came in, so it is not income and probably was not his expense either** |
| **nothing in 2025** | 🔴 **the insurer paid in 2026** ⇒ **the gain is a 2026 item and the casualty may not belong on this return at all** |

⛔ **ONE CAUTION ON METHOD: the 2025 credits already inventoried include a 13,035 `Robinhood` transfer and two
`HUNTINGTON BP` credits of 15,000 and 13,216 whose nature is NOT established** *(§3E ⑤)*. ⚠️ **None is
insurance-shaped, but do not assume a credit is the settlement because its size is convenient** — 🔑 **match
it by caption AND date, the way §3P matched the lenders.**

### ① ✅ THE SAFETY CHECK SHE ASKED FOR, RUN — AND THERE IS A TRAP IN IT

✅ **CONFIRMED: the `2015 Utility TRL` is NOT among the eight assets on the filed 2024 Form 4562.** The eight
are `FRT'18 (HU4577)` · `AUDI` · `2018 FREIGHTLINER #7107` · `#1800` · `2019 Wabash Trailer` ·
`2023 Utility Trailer` · `2022 Frght Cascadia` · `2025 Benson` *(§3A-bis)*. ⇒ **It is not on the schedule and
nothing about it is being overlooked in ATX.**

🛑 **BUT THE TRAP IS REAL AND IT IS WHY THIS CHECK MATTERS: THERE ARE TWO UTILITY TRAILERS.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **`2023 Utility Trailer`** | **IS on the schedule at 59,299**, financed by Financial Pacific, paid all year. 🔑 **IT STAYS. Do not dispose of it** |
| 🔴 **`2015 Utility TRL`** | **On NEITHER filed return**, no lender, sold 2025-06-01 for **4,000** |

⛔ **NEVER write *"the utility trailer"* unqualified on this client** — the same trap the two Benson trailers
already set.

### ② ✅ WHAT TO DO, AND IT IS THE SAME ANSWER ON EVERY PLAUSIBLE HISTORY

🔑 **The question looks open and is not, because a 2015 trailer on a five-year life is FULLY DEPRECIATED BY
2020 whether or not anyone recorded it — and §1245 recapture turns on depreciation *allowed OR ALLOWABLE*.**

| How it might have happened | Basis at the 2025 sale | The gain |
|---|---|---|
| **The company bought it and expensed the purchase** *(or §179'd it)* | **ZERO** | **4,000, ORDINARY under §1245** |
| **The company bought it and simply never recorded it** | **ZERO** — cost less allowable depreciation, and a 2015 five-year asset is fully written off by 2020 | **4,000, ORDINARY under §1245** |
| ⚠️ **The SHAREHOLDER owned it, not the company** | ⛔ **not the company's sale at all** | **the 4,000 is a CONTRIBUTION, equity side** |

⇒ ☑️ **KEY IT AS: proceeds 4,000, basis ZERO, ORDINARY income on Form 4797 Part II.** ✅ **Two of the three
histories give exactly that and neither needs a document.** ⚠️ **The third is the only alternative, it is
Julia's call and not the client's, and it moves 4,000 from income to equity — which is a real difference but
a small one.**

🔑 **AND THE POSITION IS DEFENSIBLE WITHOUT ANY DOCUMENT**, which is the point: ⛔ **we are not claiming a
basis we cannot prove; we are claiming ZERO, which is the least favourable assumption available.**
☑️ **A reviewer's objection to this row can only be that we were too conservative.**

⚠️ **WHAT JULIA SHOULD SEE, and it is why this section exists:** **the asset was sold by a company whose books
never carried it, and his own sheet assigns it a *"2023 value"* of 15,000 and a *"2024 value"* of 12,000.**
⛔ **Those are his ESTIMATES OF WORTH, not cost and not basis** — **they must never be keyed as basis, and a
reviewer glancing at his sheet could easily take the 12,000 for one.**

## 3BH · 🗣️ FORM 4562, EXPLAINED STEP BY STEP — and the DENSITY was the defect, not the reader

> **Lilian, 2026-09-28:** *"necesito que me ayudes a entender a qué te refieres con los errores en la Forma
> 4562. Necesito explicaciones más detalladas, más simples. No consigo que me expliques de forma que pueda
> entender fácilmente. Siento que tus explicaciones son muy densas, a veces escuetas, te saltas pasos y
> siento todo como en una nebulosa… pierdo mucho tiempo tratando de entenderte."*

🛑 **THIS IS A DEFECT IN THE DELIVERY AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE.** ⛔ **Every figure in §3AY and §3AX row 2 was
correct; not one of them was usable.** 🔑 **The failure is a FORM failure: the findings were written as a
register for someone who already knew the answer, and she is at the ATX keyboard, which is a different job.**

### ① ✅ THE SHAPE EVERY FINDING ON A COMPUTED FORM MUST TAKE — five steps, in this order, no exceptions

| Step | The question it answers | ⛔ What breaks it |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **What does the return show TODAY?** One figure, with its form, page, part and line | Giving the corrected figure first, so she cannot find the row she is looking at |
| **2** | **What MADE it show that?** The input, the checkbox, the attribute — **the cause inside the software** | Naming the tax rule here. She cannot type a rule |
| **3** | **Why is that wrong?** ONE sentence, **no code section in it** | Three clauses and a citation |
| **4** | **What do I type, and where?** The screen, the field, the value | *"Correct the classification"* — which is not an instruction |
| **5** | **What moves when I type it?** The lines that change, and by how much | Leaving her to work out whether it mattered |

⛔ **NEVER OPEN WITH THE AUTHORITY.** 🔑 **The IRS quote is EVIDENCE and it belongs at the END or in a
footnote.** **Opening with §280F or a Pub. 946 table is exactly what produces the fog** — it answers a
question she did not ask, before answering the one she did.

⚠️ **AND A SECOND RULE, FROM THE SAME MESSAGE: *"te saltas pasos."*** ✅ **A chain of three causes gets THREE
sentences, not one sentence with two implications in it.** ⛔ **A session that has held the chain for an hour
cannot feel where the steps are missing. Write every link.**

### ② 🔑 THE SITUATION IN ONE PARAGRAPH — before any detail at all

**Form 4562 is the depreciation form. On this return it is wrong in three places, and TWO OF THE THREE COME
FROM ONE SINGLE CHECKBOX.** ⛔ **None of them is a mis-typed number** — the arithmetic on this return is
clean. **They are all classification: an asset was told what it IS, the software believed it, and the
software then computed correctly from a wrong description.** ⇒ ✅ **So the fixes are attribute changes on
asset records, not figures to overwrite.**

### ③ 🔴 ERROR 1 — EIGHT TRUCKS AND TRAILERS ARE MARKED AS "LISTED PROPERTY", AND NONE OF THEM IS ONE

**Step 1 — what the return shows today.** Form 4562 **Part V** (page 2) lists **NINE vehicles** *(§3AW ⑧,
page 19)*: `2018 FREIGHTLINER #1800` · `2018 FREIGHTLINER #7107` · `2019 Wabash Trailer` ·
`2022 Frght Cascadia` · `2023 Utility Trailer` · `2025 Benson` · `2026 Reitnouer DropMiser Trailer` ·
`AUDI` · `FRT'18(HU4577)`. 🔑 **All nine carry the attribute. Only THREE of them are visibly CAPPED:**

| Asset | Cost | 2025 depreciation ON THE RETURN |
|---|---|---|
| `2026 Reitnouer DropMiser Trailer` *(in service 3/5/2025)* | 70,540 | **20,200** *(as bonus)* |
| `2022 Frght Cascadia` *(in service 9/25/2024)* | 85,500 | **19,800** |
| `2025 Benson` *(in service 9/25/2024)* | 67,050 | **19,800** |

**Step 2 — what made it show that.** In the ATX asset record, each asset has an attribute that says whether
it is **listed property** (it prints on this return as `V-7`). **That attribute is set on all NINE.**
⚠️ **The other six are not capped only because their remaining basis is already zero or small — the wrong
attribute is on them just the same, and it is what puts them in the mileage table.**
**When it is set, ATX routes the asset to Part V of Form 4562, and Part V applies the passenger-automobile
dollar limit.** ⇒ 🔑 **The deduction then stops at a fixed table amount instead of being computed from cost.**

**Step 3 — why that is wrong.** **Those limits exist only for cars.** A Freightliner Cascadia is a Class-8
tractor and a Benson or Reitnouer is a semi-trailer — **a trailer is not even a self-propelled vehicle.**

**Step 3b — how you can SEE it without doing any arithmetic, and this is the part worth keeping.**
🔑 **The `2022 Frght Cascadia` cost 85,500 and the `2025 Benson` cost 67,050 — different costs — and the
return gives BOTH of them the same two numbers: prior accumulated depreciation 12,400 and 2025 depreciation
19,800.** ⛔ **Two assets of different cost cannot produce identical depreciation by calculation.**
⇒ ✅ **Identical figures on unequal costs are always a CAP and never a computation.** *(12,400 is the 2024
first-year car limit where bonus is not taken; 19,800 the second-year limit. The Reitnouer's 20,200 is the
2025 first-year limit with bonus.)*

**Step 4 — what to type.** ⛔ **NOT just the three capped ones — ALL EIGHT.** **ATX → asset detail → turn
OFF listed property on `#1800`, `#7107`, the `2019 Wabash Trailer`, the `2022 Frght Cascadia`, the
`2023 Utility Trailer`, the `2025 Benson`, the `2026 Reitnouer DropMiser Trailer` and `FRT'18(HU4577)`.**
✅ **Leave ONLY the `AUDI` as listed property.** ⇒ **The three capped ones start depreciating from their own
cost, and all eight leave the mileage table.**
🛑 🆕 **CAUGHT IN REVIEW 2026-09-28: an earlier version of this step said *"open each of those three"* while
promising the effect of eight.** ⛔ **Keying it that way leaves FIVE vehicles in Part V still reporting zero
miles, so Error 3 below would not be fixed and the *"only the Audi remains"* in step 4 there would be
false.** ✅ **No figure was at risk — the other five carry no cap — but the ACTION was wrong, which is the
half she works from.**

**Step 5 — what moves.** ⚠️ **Computed with the 2025 bonus REMOVED, which is where the return now stands:**

| Asset | What it takes once it is out of Part V | On the return now | 💵 Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2026 Reitnouer` 70,540 | **70,540 × 20% = 14,108** *(5-year, 200DB, half-year, first year)* | **12,200** *(the no-bonus 2025 car cap it falls to once bonus is off)* | **+1,908** |
| `2022 Frght Cascadia` 85,500 | **85,500 × 32% = 27,360** *(5-year, year two)* | **19,800** | **+7,560** |
| `2025 Benson` 67,050 | **67,050 × 32% = 21,456** *(5-year, year two)* | **19,800** | **+1,656** |
| | | ⇒ **TOTAL** | 🔴 **≈ +11,124 of depreciation** |

⚠️ **ONE CAVEAT, AND IT IS SEPARATE FROM THIS FIX: the `2022 Frght Cascadia`'s 5-year LIFE is itself an open
question** *(§3AO ⑤ — over-the-road tractors are 3-year property under Pub. 946 class 00.26)*. ⛔ **Do not
change it here.** 🔑 **It went on the FILED 2024 return at five years, so changing it is a prior-year method
question and it is JULIA's** *(§3AX row 2's note; FOLLOW-UPS row 130)*. ✅ **The figures above deliberately
keep the life the return already uses, so this fix stands on its own.**

⚠️ **AND THE SAME CHECKBOX ALSO CAUSES ERROR 3 BELOW** — which is why two of the three errors close together.

📄 **The authority, LAST and not first — Instructions for Form 4562 (2025)**, downloaded 2026-09-27 from
`irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4562.pdf`, page proof 30-Mar-2026, verbatim:
> *"Passenger automobiles are 4-wheeled vehicles manufactured primarily for use on public roads that are
> rated at 6,000 pounds unloaded gross vehicle weight or less (for a truck or van, gross vehicle weight is
> substituted for unloaded gross vehicle weight)."*

### ④ 🔴 ERROR 2 — THE DESTROYED TRUCK IS STILL ON THE DEPRECIATION SCHEDULE

**Step 1 — what the return shows today.** `2018 FREIGHTLINER #7107`, cost 78,145, **is still listed as an
owned asset** on the Form 4562 detail and on page 21's UBIA listing, and its cost is inside Schedule L lines
10a and 10b. **Form 4797 line 14 is blank and there is no Form 4684 on the return at all.**

**Step 2 — what made it show that.** **Nothing was ever entered to dispose of it.** 🔑 **`#7107` is unit
`1835`, the truck that was totalled** *(decision 61 and §3AP ⑥)*.

**Step 3 — why that is wrong.** **A destroyed asset stops being an asset, and the money received for it is a
gain that has to be reported.**

> ⛔ 🆕 **THIS SUB-SECTION IS SUPERSEDED IN TWO PLACES — 2026-09-28. READ §3BL ② FIRST.**
> 🔴 **THE ROUTING IS WRONG: `#7107` took 50,000 of §179, and an S-corporation does NOT report the disposal
> of §179 property on its own Form 4797 or Form 4684. It goes to the SHAREHOLDER on K-1 BOX 17 CODE K
> (now 24,500), and page 1 line 4 does NOT move** *(decision 87; ATX warns on screen in red)*.
> 📅 **AND THE DATE IS NOW `04/09/2025`, not `01/01/2025`** *(decision 86, Lilian's own — and PROVISIONAL
> until the client answers)*. ✅ **Everything else below — the involuntary-conversion disposition type,
> the ZERO adjusted basis, and entering ONLY the truck's share — is right and is what she keyed.**

**Step 4 — what to type.** **ATX → asset detail → `#7107` → dispose of it as an INVOLUNTARY CONVERSION.**
🔑 **That routing is what puts it on Form 4684 Section B instead of an ordinary sale** — ⛔ 🆕 **except on THIS asset, which took §179 and therefore goes to K-1 box 17K with Form 4684 left empty** *(decision 87)*.
- **Date of disposition: `01/01/2025`** — ✅ **decision 82 settles this and ⑥ below explains why.**
- **Adjusted basis: ZERO.** 🔑 **The whole 78,145 was already deducted — 50,000 of §179 plus 28,145 of bonus
  in its first year** *(§3A-bis)*. ⇒ **There is nothing left to write off.**
- **Proceeds: ONLY the truck's share — on the client's own figures about 20,000.** ⛔ **NOT 57,500.** **The
  tow money is a different thing and ⑤ below says where it goes.**

**Step 5 — what moves.** 🔑 **Because the basis is zero, every dollar entered as proceeds is gain, and it is
§1245 ORDINARY income** *(not capital)*. ⇒ **page 1 line 4 rises by roughly 20,000.** ⚠️ **Schedule L 10a and
10b each fall by 78,145, so TOTAL assets do not move** — **what changes is that a destroyed truck stops
appearing as something the company owns.**

⚠️ **Related and NOT part of this entry: the `2015 Utility Trailer` sold 6/1/2025 for 4,000 is also absent**
*(§3AX row 4, decision 67)*. **It was never capitalized, so it goes straight onto Form 4797 Part II line 10 —
gross 4,000, cost 0, depreciation 0 — and NOT onto the depreciation schedule.**

### ⑤ 🟡 ERROR 3 — NINE VEHICLES REPORT ZERO MILES, AND TWO QUESTIONS ARE UNANSWERED

**Step 1 — what the return shows today.** **Form 4562 Part V Section B lists nine vehicles with 0 business
miles, 0 commuting miles and 0 personal miles**, and **lines 24a and 24b — *"Do you have evidence to support

**Step 2 — what made it show that.** **The same listed-property attribute as Error 1 put nine vehicles into

**Step 3 — why that is wrong.** **A trucking company reporting zero business miles on every vehicle is the

**Step 4 — what to type.** ✅ **Error 1's fix — DONE ON ALL EIGHT, not just the three capped ones — removes

8/21/2025)*, **and answer 24a and 24b.** ⚠️ **If no mileage record exists, that is itself the finding and it

**Step 5 — what moves.** **No figure on the return changes.** 🔑 **This one is exposure, not arithmetic.**

### ⑥ 🔵 AND THE FOURTH THING ON THIS FORM IS NOT 2025's TO FIX — Lilian ruled on it

| **3** | **Enter the Audi's real 2025 miles and answer 24a / 24b** | minutes | **nothing — it removes an exposure** |

### ② 🛑 BUT REMOVING THE BONUS IN THE ASSET RECORDS IS **HALF** THE JOB — the other half is an ELECTION

📄 **Instructions for Form 4562 (2025)**, `irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4562.pdf`, page proof 30-Mar-2026, verbatim:

> *"**Election out.** You can elect, for any class of property, to not deduct any special depreciation
> allowance for all such property in such class placed in service during the tax year. To make an election,
> **attach a statement to your timely filed return (including extensions)** indicating the class of property
> for which you are making the election and that, for such class, you are not to claim any special
> depreciation allowance."*

⇒ ✅ 🆕 **AND BOTH WERE ALREADY SATISFIED — decision 93: the statement is on PAGE 20 and names six classes, including the two this return needs. What follows is why it matters, not what is owed.** _(As written:)_ 🔴 **TWO CONSEQUENCES, AND BOTH ARE EASY TO MISS BECAUSE THE RETURN LOOKS RIGHT WITHOUT THEM:**

| | What it means here |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **The STATEMENT is mandatory** | **Turning bonus off asset by asset produces the correct FIGURES with no valid election behind them.** ⇒ ☑️ **ATX → `Elections` page → the §168(k) election-out statement, for 2025.** ⚠️ **It is ANNUAL — a 2024 election does nothing for 2025** *(§3A-bis ④)* |
| 🔴 **It is made BY CLASS, for ALL property in that class** | ⛔ **You cannot elect out for some assets and keep bonus on others within the same recovery period.** **Zakom's 2025 additions span TWO classes** ⇒ **the statement must name BOTH** |

**The two classes, and what is in each:**

| Class | Assets | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **3-year** *(over-the-road tractors, Pub. 946 class 00.26)* | the four 2025 tractors | **307,295** |
| **5-year** | `2022 Benson` trailer **43,650** + `2026 Reitnouer` trailer **70,540** | **114,190** |

⚠️ **CHECK THIS AFTER SHE RE-KEYS: if any 2025 asset still carries bonus, the election for its class is
inconsistent with the return and one of the two has to move.** 🔑 **"Todos los vehículos" should mean all six
additions, but the trailers are not vehicles in ordinary speech and are the easiest to leave behind.**

ⓘ **Once made, the election cannot be revoked without IRS consent** *(same page)*. ✅ **Not a problem — it is
the position she chose — but it means the statement is not a formality to add later.**

### ⑤ 🔑 HOW THE TOW MONEY IS REPORTED — her third question, and it depends on ONE fact

> **Lilian, 2026-09-28:** *"necesito saber cómo reportar ese dinero de la grúa, ese reembolso que se pagó por
> la grúa, ¿cómo se reporta?"*

**Start from what the tow money is NOT.** ⛔ **It is not proceeds for the truck**, so ⛔ **it never goes on
Form 4684 and it never goes in the asset disposition** *(§3AU ① — this is the point she herself made on
2026-09-27 and it was right)*. ✅ **Form 4684 takes the reimbursement received **for the property**, nothing
else.**

🔑 **WHAT IT IS: the recovery of an EXPENSE. And a recovered expense follows ONE rule — it is income only if
the expense was deducted.** ⇒ **So there are exactly two outcomes, and the fact that decides between them is
whether the ≈34,000 tow is inside a 2025 deduction:**

| If the tow… | Then the reimbursement is… | 🛠️ **Where it goes** |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ **was DEDUCTED in 2025** *(it would be inside `Auto Repars & Maintenance`, 54,032)* | **INCOME** | **Net it against the same caption — reduce `Auto Repars & Maintenance` by the tow amount.** ⓘ **Same year, same character; page 1 line 5 as other income gives the identical result if she prefers to show it gross** |
| ✅ **was NEVER deducted** *(the company never bore the cost)* | ⛔ **NOT income. Nothing is entered** | **Both sides cancel and the return says nothing about it** |

🛑 **THE TWO SIDES MUST MATCH OR THE RETURN IS WRONG IN ONE DIRECTION OR THE OTHER.** ⛔ **Deducting the tow
and not reporting its recovery understates income by ≈34,000; reporting the recovery without the deduction
overstates it by the same.**

#### 🔵 AND THE EVIDENCE WE ALREADY HOLD POINTS AT THE SECOND ROW — three independent readings

> 🔴 **NARROWED 2026-09-30, AND IT MATTERS NOW THAT THE LOSS IS DATED `12/17/2024`.** **All three readings

> reaches whether the tow was deducted on the **2024** return, which is the live question once the truck is
> known to have been destroyed in December 2024** *(§3CD ④)*. ☑️ **The free check is the 2024 return's own
> page 1 line 20 attached statement.** ⚠️ **And readings 1 and 2 look on a card and a bank account his own
> sheet says he did NOT use — *"cash using business line of credit"*, §3AU ⑦ — so their silence is rule 1b's
> error in miniature: it belongs to the search that produced it.**

1. ⛔ **It is not on the Amex, in either year** *(§3BF, decision 77 — 406 charges totalling 114,023.00 in
   2025, largest single 6,931.39; eleven towing/recovery merchants totalling 3,396.71)*.
2. ⛔ **No SINGLE debit of that size left the operating account.** **The only debits of 15,000 or more all
   year are the 34,000 Amex payment and a 16,500 wire** *(§3BD; decision 78)*. ⚠️ **State it at the search's
   own width, not wider** *([`method.md`](../../pre-return-review/method.md) rule 1b)*: **the search was
   bounded at 15,000, so three instalments of ~11,000 would not have been seen.**

🔑 **A gain on property destroyed in a casualty can be DEFERRED under §1033 if replacement property is
bought**, and **Zakom bought 307,295 of tractors in the same year.** ⇒ **The ≈20,000 casualty gain could
legally be rolled into their basis instead of reported.**

⛔ **RECOMMENDED AGAINST, and the reason is the same one that drove decision 3:**

  ≈23,500 LOSS** — **and the shareholder's basis is what limits a loss, with the AAA opening at zero.**
  ⇒ **A deferred gain would likely buy a loss he cannot deduct.**
- **It reduces the new tractors' depreciable basis by the deferred amount**, so the deduction comes back
  over three years anyway.
- **It requires its own election statement with the return** and locks the position.

☑️ **RAISED, NOT DECIDED — it is JULIA's if anyone wants it** *(decision 83)*. ⛔ **Do not key a §1033
deferral without her.**

### ① 🔑 RETAINED EARNINGS vs ADDITIONAL PAID-IN CAPITAL — the names, the difference, and what actually changes

**The two account names, in English, exactly as they print on Schedule L:**

| Line | Name on the form | What it is supposed to hold |
|---|---|---|
| **23** | **`Additional paid-in capital`** *(APIC)* | 🔑 **Money the SHAREHOLDER PUT IN, above the nominal price of his shares.** It is *his* contribution — capital, not profit |
| **24** | **`Retained earnings`** | 🔑 **Profit the company MADE and has not yet paid out.** When it is negative it is an *accumulated deficit* |

🔑 **THE DIFFERENCE IN ONE SENTENCE: paid-in capital is money that came IN FROM the owner; retained
earnings is money the company EARNED.** ⇒ **They answer two different questions, and a distribution —
money going OUT to the owner — could logically be charged against either.**

#### ⓐ ✅ WHAT THE 2024 RETURN PRINTS — three figures and one exact identity

| Where on the 2024 return | What it prints |
|---|---|
| **Schedule K line 16d** *(and its statement)* — total distributions | **113,157** |
| **Schedule M-2 line 7** — what ran through the AAA | **51,988** |
| **Schedule L line 23** — additional paid-in capital | **(61,169)** |
| **Schedule M-2 line 8** — closing AAA | **ZERO** |
| **Schedule L line 24** — retained earnings | **blank** |

✅ `113,157 − 51,988 = 61,169`, **to the dollar.** 🔑 **So: the AAA absorbed as much of the distribution as
it had and went to zero, and the remainder — the part the AAA could not absorb — equals the negative
paid-in-capital figure exactly.**

🛑 **AND THIS PAPER'S STANDING BAN APPLIES, so read the sentence above carefully.** ⛔ **What is stated is
what the return PRINTS and an arithmetic identity between three printed numbers.** ⛔ **It is NOT stated
as "what the preparer decided to do" — nobody has asked her** *(§3AE ②, §3A, §3I ③; decision 51 is Lilian
deferring exactly that question on 2026-09-27)*. ⚠️ **Lilian's message says *"¿Qué fue lo que Julia hizo en 2020?"* — read as 2024**, which is the year the
firm holds and the year that feeds 2025's opening column. ⛔ **No 2020 return is in the firm's hands.**

#### ⓑ 🔑 WHAT CHANGES IF YOU PICK ONE OR THE OTHER — the honest answer is *almost nothing*

⛔ **NEITHER LINE CHANGES ONE NUMBER OF TAX.** **Schedule L is the balance sheet per books. Neither
retained earnings nor paid-in capital touches:**

- **taxable income** *(page 1 line 22)*,
- **the AAA** *(Schedule M-2)*,
- **what goes on the K-1**,
- **the shareholder's stock basis**, or
- **how the distribution is taxed to him** *(that is decided by §1368 — AAA first, then basis, then capital gain — and it runs off the M-2 and his own basis schedule, not off Schedule L)*.

✅ **The distribution itself is reported the same way either way: Schedule K line 16d and K-1 box 16d carry
the FULL figure.** 🔑 **The only question is which equity line on the BALANCE SHEET absorbs it.**

**So here is the same 105,243 keyed both ways, and both balance:**

| | Capital stock | Additional paid-in capital | Retained earnings | Total equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ⚖️ **Option A — charge it to retained earnings** | 1,000 | **(61,169)** *(carried forward, untouched)* | 🔑 **(103,550)** | **−163,719** |
| ⚖️ **Option B — charge it to paid-in capital** *(what the 2024 figures show)* | 1,000 | 🔑 **(166,412)** | **1,693** *(the book/AAA figure, untouched)* | **−163,719** |

✅ **Both equal the −163,719 the balance sheet requires** *(§3BL ③)*. ✅ **And Option B's (166,412) is just
2024's (61,169) plus this year's 105,243 — the same pattern continued.**

**What DOES differ, and it is three things, none of them tax:**

1. 🔑 **CONSISTENCY WITH THE PRIOR RETURN.** **2025's opening column must equal 2024's closing column, and
   it does — (61,169) in paid-in capital, retained earnings blank.** ⇒ **Option B continues that line;
   Option A starts a second one and leaves the first frozen.**
2. ⚠️ **WHAT THE BALANCE SHEET SAYS TO A READER.** **A negative `Retained earnings` is completely ordinary
   — it is an accumulated deficit and every reader knows what it means.** **A negative
   `Additional paid-in capital` is unusual: paid-in capital is what the owner PUT IN, and it going to
   (166,412) says, on its face, that he took out far more than he ever contributed.** ⛔ **That is not
   *wrong* — it is a presentation choice some preparers use when they treat the excess as a return of
   capital — but it is the version a bank or a reviewer stops on.**
3. ☑️ **WHAT THE NEXT PREPARER INHERITS.** **Whichever line is used becomes 2026's opening column.**

⇒ ✅ 🆕 **CORRECTED 2026-09-28 — IT IS JULIA'S CALL TO CONFIRM OR OVERTURN, NOT A GATE.** **Option B is keyed and Schedule L balances** *(decision 104, §3BW ⑤)*. _(As written:)_ 🛑 IT IS JULIA'S CALL, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING ON THIS RETURN THAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS FILING.
✅ **The safe default is Option B — it matches 2024 and changes nothing about how the two returns read
together.** ⚠️ **If she prefers Option A she should say so once, for both this year and the presentation
going forward.**

### ② ✅ THE 80% MEALS RULE — what it is, what "hours of service" means, and whether this client qualifies

**Step 1 — what the return shows today.** **The line-20 statement reads `Meals, subject to 50% limit
13,714` → `Less disallowed 6,857` → `Total meals and entertainment 6,857`.** **The 6,857 also appears at
Schedule M-1 line 3b, Schedule M-2 line 5, Schedule K 16c and K-1 box 16C.**

**Step 2 — what the rule actually is.** **The default for business meals is that you deduct HALF.**
**There is one exception that matters to a trucking company, and it is not a judgement call — it is a
list of occupations.**

📄 **Publication 463 (2025), chapter 2, page proof 27-Feb-2026, VERBATIM:**

> *"**Individuals subject to "hours of service" limits.** You can deduct a higher percentage of your meal
> expenses while traveling away from your tax home if the meals take place during or incident to any
> period subject to the Department of Transportation's "hours of service" limits. **The percentage is
> 80%.**
> Individuals subject to the Department of Transportation's "hours of service" limits include the
> following persons.
> • Certain air transportation workers (such as pilots, crew, dispatchers, mechanics, and control tower
> operators) who are under Federal Aviation Administration regulations.
> • **Interstate truck operators and bus drivers who are under Department of Transportation
> regulations.**
> • Certain railroad employees… • Certain merchant mariners…"*

**Step 3 — what "DOT hours of service limits" MEANS, because the name explains nothing.**

🔑 **It is a SAFETY rule, not a tax rule.** **The Department of Transportation caps how long a commercial
driver may drive before he must stop and rest** — **so many hours driving, so many hours on duty, then a
mandatory off-duty break.** **A driver under those caps physically cannot get home for dinner: the law
makes him stop and sleep away from home.** ⇒ 🔑 **Congress allowed him a bigger meal deduction precisely
because the rest rules FORCE him to eat on the road.** ⛔ **It has nothing to do with the size of the
company, the type of truck, or how the meals were paid for.**

**The test is therefore two questions, both factual:**

| | The question | For this client |
|---|---|---|
| **a** | **Is the person subject to DOT hours-of-service rules?** — an **interstate** truck operator under DOT regulations | 🟢 **The evidence is ON THE RETURN: 20,966 of `IFTA/HUT/Permits/IRP`.** **IFTA and IRP exist ONLY for operating across state lines** — a purely local carrier needs neither. **The fleet is Class-8 over-the-road tractors with sleeper-equipped units, and §3AO classifies four of them under Pub. 946 class 00.26, "Tractor Units for Use OVER-THE-ROAD"** |
| **b** | **Did the meals take place while traveling away from the tax home, during or incident to such a period?** | 🟡 **Not established document by document.** **13,714 over a year of interstate running is consistent, but nobody has tied the meals to trips** |

**Step 4 — so can he take 80%? And what to type.**

✅ **On the law: YES, the company qualifies on test (a), and the evidence for it is already printed on its
own return.** ⛔ **BUT THERE IS A SECOND QUESTION THAT IS NOT ABOUT THE RATE AT ALL, AND IT IS JULIA'S:**

🛑 **WHOSE MEALS ARE IN THE 13,714?** 🔑 **The six drivers are 1099 CONTRACTORS, not employees.**
⇒ ⛔ **A contractor's own meals are HIS deduction on HIS return, not the company's** — **the company can
only deduct meals it actually bore for its own people** *(the owner-driver)* **or that it reimbursed under
an arrangement it can support.** ⚠️ **If most of the 13,714 is drivers' meals, the rate is the wrong
argument and the whole line needs looking at** *(this is §3BA's open half, and it was already routed to
Julia rather than the client)*.

☑️ **IF Julia agrees to 80%, what to type:** **in the line-20 statement change the meals limit from 50% to
80%.** ⇒ **Line 1e `Less disallowed` becomes 2,743** *(`13,714 × 20%`)* **and line 1f becomes 10,971.**
**Then CHECK these follow, because they all carry the same figure: page 1 line 20 → 1,098,537 · Schedule
M-1 line 3b → 2,743 · Schedule M-2 line 5 → 2,743 · Schedule K 16c → 2,743 · K-1 box 16C → 2,743.**

**Step 5 — what it moves.** 💵 **+4,114 of deduction, in the client's favour.**

#### ⚠️ AND ON *"2024 USED 50%, SO 50% IS SAFER"* — the honest answer, because she asked for it

✅ **She is right that 50% is the safe answer, and right to want Julia to decide.** ☑️ **Three things that
belong in that decision:**

1. ⛔ **50% is not *wrong* — it is a smaller deduction than the law allows, which is never a penalty
   risk.** **Nobody is examined for deducting too little.**
2. ⚠️ **But it is not free either: it is 4,114 a year the client does not get, every year, and 2024 had
   the same facts.**
3. 🔑 **THE REAL REASON THIS ONE IS NOT OBVIOUS IS NOT THE RATE — IT IS *(b)* AND THE CONTRACTOR
   QUESTION.** ⇒ ☑️ **Put BOTH to Julia together: *"the company qualifies for 80% on the face of the
   return; before we take it, whose meals are these?"*** ⛔ **Taking 80% on meals that are the
   contractors' own would be the wrong answer at a better rate.**

### ③ ⛔ SCHEDULE K LINE 14b — she is right to push, and my earlier advice was too simple

> **Lilian, 2026-09-28:** *"¿Por qué dices que debo marcar la línea 14B en el Schedule K? No entiendo eso.
> No veo que en el año 2024 se haya hecho eso."*

🛑 **§3AX row 14 said *"Tick 14b (the domestic-filing exception) unless something international exists."*
THAT IS WITHDRAWN. It is not a box you simply tick.**

📄 **Instructions for Form 1120-S (2025), page 37, page proof 15-Jan-2026, VERBATIM:**

> *"Check the box on line 14a if you are reporting items of international tax relevance… **If you satisfy
> the domestic filing exception to filing Schedule K-3, you must provide notification to the shareholder
> either through an attachment to the Schedule K-1 or a separate statement prior to filing the Form
> 1120-S.** Check the box on line 14b if you satisfy an exception to filing Schedule K-2 (Form 1120-S).
> **Attach a statement to explain your qualification for the exception.**"*

⇒ 🔑 **TICKING 14b CARRIES TWO OBLIGATIONS, AND NEITHER HAS BEEN DONE:**

| | What ticking 14b requires |
|---|---|
| **1** | **A NOTIFICATION TO THE SHAREHOLDER**, given **before the return is filed** — attached to his K-1 or sent separately — telling him he will not receive a Schedule K-3 unless he asks for one |
| **2** | **A STATEMENT ATTACHED TO THE RETURN** explaining why the corporation qualifies for the exception |

⇒ ⛔ **So ticking it today would assert something that is not yet true.** ✅ **The box is not a correction
— it is a small procedure.**

**What line 14a and 14b are actually FOR, in plain terms:** **Schedules K-2 and K-3 are the international
pages of an S-corp return. Even a company with no foreign activity can be pulled into filing them, because
a SHAREHOLDER may need the information for his own foreign-tax-credit form.** **The "domestic filing
exception" exists to let an ordinary domestic company out of that — and the price of it is telling the
shareholder, in advance, that no K-3 is coming.**

☑️ **WHAT TO DO — and both answers are defensible:**

| | Route | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ **A** | **Leave 14a and 14b BLANK, as 2024 did** | **Not an error.** ⚠️ **It leaves the exception unclaimed on the face of the return** |
| ⚖️ **B** | **Tick 14b AND do the two things above** — the notification attached to the K-1, and the explanatory statement | **Documents the exception.** ☑️ **Both are easy at filing time** |

🔑 **RECOMMENDATION: A, matching 2024** — ⛔ **the consistency argument she raised is the right one, and it
is stronger than the marginal protection B buys for a single-shareholder domestic company with zero
foreign activity.** ☑️ **Raise B with Julia as a firm-wide habit rather than as a fix to this return.**
✅ **Line 14a stays blank either way — nothing on this return is of international relevance.**

**What it means.** **§199A is the 20% qualified-business-income deduction.** **An S corporation does not
take it — the SHAREHOLDER does, on his own 1040 — but the corporation has to hand him the numbers.**

📄 **Instructions for Form 1120-S (2025), page proof 15-Jan-2026, verbatim:**
> *"S corporations should use **Statement A—QBI Pass-Through Entity Reporting**, or a substantially
> similar statement, to report each shareholder's pro rata information from each trade or business,
> including QBI items, W-2 wages, UBIA of qualified property… **by attaching the completed statement(s) to
> each shareholder's Schedule K-1.**"*
> *"**Section 199A information (code V).**"*

**What the return shows today.** ⛔ **K-1 box 17 carries only code K (24,500) and code AC (1,092,014).
There is NO code V and NO Statement A.**

🛠️ **WHAT TO TYPE.** **ATX → the `Sec 199A Activities` worksheet → mark the trucking activity as a
QUALIFIED trade or business, and NOT a specified service trade or business (SSTB).** ⇒ **ATX then builds
Statement A and fills K-1 box 17 code V with three figures:**

| On Statement A | For this client |
|---|---|
| **Ordinary business income (loss) — the QBI** | **the page 1 line 22 figure** *(§3BP ③ tracks where it lands)* |
| **W-2 wages** | 🔑 **ZERO — the company paid no wages** *(page 1 lines 7 and 8 are both blank, and the drivers are 1099)* |
| **UBIA of qualified property** | ✅ **683,334 — ATX ALREADY COMPUTES IT: it is on page 19, `Summary of Unadjusted Basis of Qualified Property`** |

🛑 **AND THE REASON IT MUST STILL BE REPORTED ON A LOSS YEAR — ⚠️ 🆕 CORRECTED IN REVIEW 2026-09-28,
because the first version of this paragraph had it BACKWARDS.**

📄 **Instructions for Form 8995 (2025), Line 4, verbatim:**
> *"**If you have a qualified business net loss for the year, you don't qualify for the QBI deduction**
> unless you have qualified REIT dividends or qualified PTP income. **The loss will be carried forward to
> next year.** This carryforward doesn't affect the deductibility of the loss for purposes of any other
> provisions of the Code."*

⇒ 🔑 **SO THE CARRYFORWARD IS ADVERSE TO HIM, NOT AN ASSET.** **A negative QBI is treated next year as a
loss from a qualified trade or business: it REDUCES next year's QBI and therefore next year's 20%
deduction.** ⛔ **It does NOT "offset income he would otherwise pay tax on" — the deduction is 20% of QBI,
and QBI is not a tax base.** *(That is what the withdrawn sentence said.)*

☑️ **THE REAL REASON TO REPORT IT, and it is enough:** **it is REQUIRED, the K-1 is incomplete without it,
and his 1040 must carry the correct carryforward.** ⇒ ⛔ **Omitting it would OVERSTATE his future
deduction** — **which is a compliance exposure on HIS return, not a saving on this one.** ⚠️ **It also has to agree with what his 1040 preparer expects,
and on this client the company and the owner are prepared by the same firm.**

### ④ 🔴 `4562` — *"Assets placed in service after 2015 electing out of bonus depreciation should use the same Fed/AMT depreciation method."*

**What it means, and it is the opposite of what most people assume.**

📄 **Instructions for Form 4562 (2025), the `Election out` block, verbatim:**
> *"**Note:** If you elect to not have any special depreciation allowance apply, the property placed in
> service during the tax year **will not be subject to an AMT adjustment for depreciation.**"*

🔑 **SO: because you elected OUT of bonus, the 2025 additions must carry the SAME depreciation for AMT as
for regular tax, and their AMT adjustment must be ZERO.** ⇒ **ATX is telling you the asset records
currently hold a different AMT method from the federal one, which would produce an adjustment that should
not exist.**

⚠️ **The corporation itself pays no AMT — the corporate AMT was repealed for tax years after 2017 — so
this changes nothing on page 1. It changes what the SHAREHOLDER gets on K-1 box 15**, *which he needs for
his own Form 6251.*

🛠️ **WHAT TO TYPE.** **ATX → asset detail → each of the SIX 2025 additions → the `Depreciation and
Section 179` tab → set the AMT method and life to match the federal ones (200DB, same recovery period).**
⇒ ☑️ **Then check K-1 box 15: it currently shows `A −1,809` and `B −3,719`, and the 2025 assets' share of
those should fall out.** ⚠️ **Do not expect box 15 to go to zero** — **the PRIOR-year assets can still
carry an adjustment of their own, and nothing here touches them.**

### ⑤ 🟡 `Fixed Assets` — *"AUDI - has different federal and state recovery basis, please review amounts for state disposition."*

**What it means.** **ATX keeps a separate STATE basis for every asset, because states often decouple from
federal bonus and §179.** **The Audi's state basis differs from its federal basis, and it was DISPOSED OF
in 2025 (8/21/2025) — so the state gain would be computed off a different number.**

🛠️ **WHAT TO DO — and the first step is a question, not a keystroke:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **1** | ☑️ **Is a STATE return part of this engagement at all?** ⛔ **There is no state form in the 20 pages of this draft** *(and the depreciation detail's state column is what ATX is warning about, not a filed form)* |
| **2** | ⚠️ **NOT ESTABLISHED EITHER WAY FOR 2024:** §3A-bis ⑤ records that the 2024 return *as extracted* showed no state return, **but that two of its pages barely extracted — so that is not evidence** *(method rule 1b)* |
| **3** | ✅ **If no state return is filed, this warning is informational and nothing is keyed.** 🔴 **If one IS filed, open the Audi's state columns and reconcile the state basis before the disposition is accepted** |

🔑 **PUT IT TO JULIA AS ONE QUESTION: does Zakom file a Florida return?** ⛔ **A session may not settle it
from the file.**

### ③ ✅ *"¿El additional paid-in capital sería algo así como las contribuciones del dueño?"* — YES, exactly

🔑 **That is precisely what it is.** **`Capital stock` is what he paid for his shares at the very
beginning — the nominal amount, 1,000 here. `Additional paid-in capital` is EVERYTHING ELSE he has put
in: money he contributed to the company without buying more shares and without lending it.**

⇒ 🛑 **WHICH IS WHY A NEGATIVE PAID-IN CAPITAL IS AN ODD THING TO PRINT, and why §3BM ①ⓑ flagged it: a
figure that is supposed to measure *what the owner PUT IN* showing (166,412) is saying he has taken out
166,412 more than he ever contributed.** ✅ **It is a presentation some preparers use for distributions in
excess of earnings, and it is what the 2024 figures show — but it is the line a bank or a reviewer stops
on.** ☑️ **Nothing about the tax changes either way** *(§3BM ①ⓑ)*.

unanswered.** ⛔ **It is not a client question and it is not a defect.** _(As written:)_ ⚠️ money the
owner puts in can also be a LOAN — a loan is not a contribution: it is repayable, it does not affect his
stock basis the same way, and it belongs on line 19 rather than line 23.

trailer is not self-propelled at all.**
