### ② 🐎 "THE FIVE RIDERS" — what that phrase was hiding

> 🗣️ *"Explícame esto despacio, que no entiendo qué tengo que hacer: los cinco jinetes juntos (17K 28,000 ·
> M-2 3/6/7 28,000/10,849/10,849, línea 8 CERO · L23 (173,912) · residual 112,743)."*

⛔ **THAT LINE SHOULD NEVER HAVE BEEN WRITTEN LIKE THAT.** ✅ **Here is the whole thing, from the beginning.**

#### ②ⓐ 🔑 THE ONE CHANGE THAT CAUSES ALL THE OTHERS

**The truck `#7107` — the client's unit `1835` — was destroyed and the insurance paid for it. The disposal is
currently keyed with `20,000` of proceeds. It should be `23,500`.** **That is the only thing being changed;
everything else is a consequence.**

```
   Insurance received                                57,500
   less the towing it reimbursed, never deducted    (34,000)
                                                   ---------
   Proceeds attributable to the TRUCK                23,500     ← what goes in the field
```
⇒ **The change is `+3,500`.** 🔑 **Follow that 3,500 through the return and every other figure falls out.**

#### ②ⓑ ☑️ WHERE THE 3,500 GOES, ONE STEP AT A TIME

**STEP 1 — the income does NOT go on the corporation's return.** **The truck was written off under §179 back
in 2021, and when a §179 asset is disposed of the gain is reported to the SHAREHOLDER, not by the company.**
**ATX says so on screen as you key it: *"This disposition will NOT be reported on the 4797 per the form
instructions. Please see report on the 179 Dispo tab on Schedule K-1."*** ⇒ **It lands on the K-1.**

**STEP 2 — `K-1 box 17, code K`.** **That box carries the §179 disposals for the year, and there are two of
them: unit `1836` at `4,500` and this truck.**
```
   1836                4,500
   #7107      20,000 → 23,500
                     ---------
   Box 17K    24,500 → 28,000
```

**STEP 3 — `Schedule M-2 line 3`.** ℹ️ **The M-2 is the running record of the company's accumulated taxable
profit — the AAA. Anything that is taxable income to the shareholder has to be added to it, or the record
stops matching the return.** **The same 28,000 goes on line 3, `Other additions`.**

**STEP 4 — `Schedule M-2 line 6` — this one COMPUTES, it is not typed.** ℹ️ **Line 6 is just the subtotal:
opening balance, plus the year's income, plus other additions, less the year's loss, less non-deductible
items.**
```
   line 1  opening AAA                          0
   line 2  ordinary income                      0      (the year is a LOSS, so it goes on line 4)
   line 3  other additions           24,500 → 28,000   ← STEP 3
   line 4  ordinary loss                  (10,294)
   line 5  non-deductible (the meals)      (6,857)
                                        -----------
   line 6  SUBTOTAL                 7,349 → 10,849
```

**STEP 5 — `Schedule M-2 line 7`, the distributions. 🔴 THIS IS THE ONE THAT GETS FORGOTTEN, AND IT IS THE
WHOLE REASON THE LIST EXISTED.** ℹ️ **A distribution cannot push the AAA below zero. So line 7 takes only as
much as line 6 is holding, and line 8 closes at zero.**
```
   line 6                     10,849
   line 7  distributions      10,849   ← it takes ALL of line 6, not the old 7,349
   line 8  closing AAA             0
```
⛔ **IF YOU CHANGE LINE 6 AND LEAVE LINE 7 AT 7,349, LINE 8 PRINTS 3,500 INSTEAD OF ZERO.** **The return does
not fail, nothing warns you, and the AAA is wrong by exactly the amount you just added.**

**STEP 6 — `Schedule L line 23`, `Additional paid-in capital`.** ℹ️ **This is where this return charges what
the owner took out. If his distributions went up 3,500, this goes down 3,500.**
```
   line 23     (170,412) → (173,912)
```

**STEP 7 — the figure reported as distributions, on `Schedule K line 16d` and `K-1 box 16d`.**
```
   109,243 → 112,743        ← 173,912 less the 61,169 of paid-in capital carried in from 2024
```
⚠️ **`112,743` IS AN INTERMEDIATE, NOT THE FIGURE THAT GETS FILED.** ⛔ **DO NOT KEY 16d UNTIL ④ IS DONE:**
**④ records the IPFS liability on Schedule L, which re-derives this whole section and takes `Schedule K
line 16d` and `K-1 box 16d` to `132,583`.** 🔑 **The 3,500 casualty correction and the IPFS entry are two
separate fixes that land on the SAME lines, so keying ② and stopping leaves the distributions 19,840 short.**

#### ②ⓒ ✅ AND THE CHECK THAT TELLS YOU IT WORKED

```
   capital stock                 1,000
   line 23 paid-in capital    (173,912)
   line 24 retained earnings    10,849
                             -----------
   CLOSING EQUITY             (162,063)

   and it must equal:  total assets 474,926 − total liabilities 636,989 = (162,063)   ✅
```
🔑 **The closing equity does NOT change when you make this correction — it was `(162,063)` before and it is
`(162,063)` after.** **That is what tells you the seven steps were done together: the 3,500 moved through the
return and came out the other side without breaking the balance sheet.**

### ③ 🏦 WHY `Schedule L line 17` GETS 20,872.61 WHEN IT HAD NOTHING BEFORE

> 🗣️ *"Explícame por qué el Schedule L línea 17 ¿Qué dice 'mortgages notes bonds payable in less than one
> year'? Debe ser ese monto de 20,872. Esto es debido a IPFS. Por favor, explícame por qué este número va en
> esa casilla donde no teníamos nada anteriormente."*

#### ③ⓐ ℹ️ WHAT SCHEDULE L IS, IN ONE SENTENCE

**It is a photograph of what the company OWNED and OWED on 31 December.** **The top half is what it owns; the
bottom half is what it owes and what is left over for the owner. The two halves have to come to the same
total.**

#### ③ⓑ 🔑 WHY THE COMPANY OWES IPFS ANYTHING AT ALL — this is the part that is not obvious

**The truck insurance costs `35,593` for the year and the carrier will not bill it monthly. So:**

```
   ZAKOM  ─── 6,336.90 down ────────────────────►  the agency  ──┐
                                                                 ├──►  THE INSURER IS PAID IN FULL,
   IPFS   ─── 29,256.10, the rest of the premium ────────────────┘      in September 2025
     ▲
     └────── ZAKOM repays IPFS 3,138.90 a month ──────
```

🛑 **SO FROM THE DAY THE POLICY STARTED, THE COMPANY DOES NOT OWE A PREMIUM. THE INSURER HAS ITS MONEY.**
**What the company owes is a LOAN, to a finance company.** ⇒ **A loan the company still owes on 31 December
is a debt, and a debt belongs on Schedule L. That is the whole reason.**

#### ③ⓒ ❓ "WHY WAS IT EMPTY BEFORE?"

⛔ **It was not an error that is now being corrected. It was a debt nobody had recognised as a debt.**
**Until this week the IPFS payments looked like an insurance payment plan — money going out monthly for
insurance. What changed is the analysis, not the facts: once you see that the insurer was paid in full at
inception, the monthly payments stop being insurance and become loan repayments, and the unpaid part becomes
a liability.** 🔑 **Nothing was missed on the balance sheet; the balance sheet was built before the question
was asked.**

#### ③ⓓ ✅ WHY LINE 17 AND NOT LINE 20

📄 **The 2025 Form 1120-S, read on irs.gov, has both:**

| Line | Caption |
|---|---|
| ✅ **17** | **`Mortgages, notes, bonds payable in less than 1 year`** |
| **20** | `Mortgages, notes, bonds payable in 1 year or more` |

**It is the same kind of debt on both lines. The only question is HOW SOON IT IS PAID OFF.** **The IPFS plan
is ten monthly payments starting October 2025, so the last one is July 2026 — every dollar still owed on
31 December 2025 is paid within twelve months.** ⇒ ✅ **LINE 17.**

⚠️ **AND THIS IS WHY THE FIVE EQUIPMENT LENDERS STAY ON LINE 20: BMO, Financial Pacific, the two Allegiant
notes and Mitsubishi are 36-, 60- and 72-month contracts, so most of what is owed on them is still owed a
year from now** *(line 20 = 469,568)*. ⛔ **IPFS is the only one that belongs on 17, and moving the others
there would be wrong.** ⓘ **The rest of the liability section is not on line 20 at all and nothing here
touches it: the AMEX sits on `line 18` at 36,921** *(decision 17)* **and the SBA loan plus the business line
of credit on `line 21` at 130,500.**

#### ③ⓔ 🧮 WHERE THE 20,872.61 COMES FROM

```
   The premium                                          35,593.00
   less the down payment the company paid itself        (6,336.90)   ← so IPFS lent 29,256.10
   less the PRINCIPAL inside the three 2025 payments    (8,383.49)
                                                       -----------
   STILL OWED TO IPFS ON 31 DECEMBER 2025               20,872.61
```

⚠️ **Note the three payments were `3,138.90` each, `9,416.70` in total — but only `8,383.49` of that reduced
the loan. The other `1,033.21` was INTEREST, and that is the figure already keyed on page 1 line 13.**
🔑 **The full month-by-month working is on the workbook sheet `How the IPFS rate was found`.**

### ④ ⚖️ WHY THE CAPITAL SECTION MOVES WHEN YOU KEY THAT LIABILITY

> 🗣️ *"¿Qué tengo que hacer con la siguiente información que me diste? '6. y la sección de capital se
> re-deriva: L23 (193,752) · M-2 6 y 7 9,816 · residual 132,583, cerrando en (182,936)'… no entiendo de dónde
> salen estos números."*

#### ④ⓐ 🔑 THE RULE THAT FORCES IT

**A balance sheet has to balance:**
```
   what the company OWNS   =   what it OWES   +   what is left for the owner
        (total assets)          (liabilities)          (equity)
```
🛑 **SO IF YOU ADD 20,872.61 OF DEBT AND TOUCH NOTHING ELSE, EQUITY HAS TO FALL BY THE SAME 20,872.61 — or
the two sides stop matching and ATX prints *"End of year balance sheet out of balance."*** ⇒ **That is why
the capital section moves. It is not a second decision; it is the same entry, seen from the other side.**

#### ④ⓑ ☑️ THE FIVE STEPS, WITH EVERY FIGURE

**STEP 1 — where we are before the change.**
```
   total assets                      474,926
   total liabilities                 636,989
   ⇒ equity must be                 (162,063)     =  474,926 − 636,989

   and it is:   capital stock            1,000
                line 23 paid-in     (173,912)
                line 24 retained       10,849
                                   ----------
                                    (162,063)     ✅
```

**STEP 2 — add the debt.**
```
   liabilities   636,989 + 20,872.61  =  657,862
   ⇒ equity must now be   474,926 − 657,862  =  (182,936)
```

**STEP 3 — the interest changes the year's result.** **The `1,033.21` of IPFS interest is a deduction, so the
year's loss gets bigger by that much, and the M-2 subtotal falls by the same.**
```
   ordinary loss    (10,294) → (11,327)
   M-2 line 6         10,849 →   9,816      (28,000 − 11,327 − 6,857)
   M-2 line 7         10,849 →   9,816      (it still takes ALL of line 6)
   M-2 line 8              0 →        0      (unchanged — it cannot go below zero)
   line 24 retained   10,849 →   9,816      (ATX computes this from the M-2)
```

**STEP 4 — the paid-in capital line absorbs what is left.** **Capital stock is fixed at 1,000 and line 24 is
computed, so line 23 is the only line that can move.**
```
   1,000  −  line 23  +  9,816   must equal  (182,936)
   ⇒ line 23  =  1,000 + 9,816 + 182,936  =  193,752      ⇒  key it as (193,752)
```

**STEP 5 — and the reported distributions follow.**
```
   line 23           193,752
   less the paid-in capital carried in from 2024   (61,169)
                    ----------
   Schedule K 16d and K-1 box 16d                  132,583
```

#### ④ⓒ ✅ THE CHECK, AND WHAT THE MOVEMENT MEANS

```
   1,000 − 193,752 + 9,816  =  (182,936)   =   474,926 − 657,862   ✅
```

🔑 **AND THE 19,839.40 THE PAID-IN CAPITAL MOVED IS NOT A PLUG — it has a name:**
```
   20,872.61   the loan still owed
    (1,033.21)  the interest already deducted inside it
   -----------
   19,839.40   = 29,256.10 IPFS lent  −  9,416.70 repaid in 2025
```
✅ **It is the part of the insurance the company DEDUCTED but has not yet PAID.** **On a set of books with no
real equity section, where everything otherwise unexplained becomes distributions, that is where it lands.**

### ⑤ 🅰️🅱️ WHAT "MODEL A" AND "MODEL B" MEAN — and the 20,000 between them

> 🗣️ *"tampoco sé con qué te refieres al modelo A y al modelo B y a esa diferencia de $20,000. No entiendo de
> qué estás hablando."*

⛔ **Those are two names this paper invented for two answers to ONE question, and the question was never
stated plainly. Here it is:**

> ❓ ***In 2025, how much of that truck insurance can the company deduct?***

| | 🅰️ **MODEL A — deduct the WHOLE PREMIUM** | 🅱️ **MODEL B — deduct only the CASH** |
|---|---|---|
| **The idea, in one line** | **The insurer was paid in full in September, so the whole year's insurance is a 2025 expense** | **A cash-basis business deducts what left the bank, and only `15,753.60` did** |
| **Insurance on page 1 line 20** | **35,593.00** | **15,753.60** |
| **Interest on page 1 line 13** | **1,033.21** | ⛔ **none — under this model the instalments ARE the insurance** |
| **Total 2025 deduction** | **36,626.21** | **15,753.60** |
| **On Schedule L** | **A debt of `20,872.61`** | ⛔ **nothing** |

🔑 **THE "DIFFERENCE OF ABOUT 20,000" IS JUST THAT SUBTRACTION:**
```
   36,626.21  −  15,753.60  =  20,872.61
```
**It is how much MORE the company deducts under A than under B. Nothing more mysterious than that.**

#### ⑤ⓐ ✅ WHICH ONE THE RETURN IS ALREADY USING — and it is not a free choice

🔑 **THE RETURN IS ALREADY ON MODEL A, and it always was — because the CLIENT'S OWN `Insurance` figure of
`79,963` contains the whole `35,593`.** ⛔ **What the return is missing is Model A's OTHER HALF: the debt.**
⚠️ **That is why this was called a DEFECT rather than a choice — the return takes A's deduction and B's
balance sheet, which is neither model.**

**And Model A is right, for two reasons that have to BOTH hold:**

1. ✅ **WAS IT PAID IN 2025?** **Yes — when someone else's money pays your bill, you have paid it. IPFS paid
   the insurer; what you owe afterwards is a loan.** 🔴 **This is the one step that rests on general
   authority rather than on a current-year IRS page, which is why it is JULIA'S to confirm.**
2. ✅ **IS IT A PREPAYMENT THAT MUST BE SPREAD OVER TWO YEARS?** **No. IRS Publication 538 lets you deduct it
   in full if the benefit does not run past 12 months from when it starts. A 12-month policy starting in
   September 2025 is exactly inside that.**

#### ⑤ⓑ 🛑 AND WHAT HAPPENS IF JULIA RULES FOR MODEL B — corrected, because an earlier version had it backwards

| | **The company's TAXABLE INCOME** | **The DISTRIBUTIONS on the K-1** |
|---|---|---|
| 🅰️ **Model A** | **deducts 36,626.21** | **132,583** |
| 🅱️ **Model B** | **deducts 15,753.60** | **132,582.40** |
| | 🔴 **20,872.61 APART** | ✅ **THE SAME, to sixty cents** |

🔑 **WHY THE DISTRIBUTIONS DO NOT MOVE, which is genuinely surprising: Model A's extra DEDUCTION and Model
A's extra DEBT are the same number.** **More deduction pushes equity down through the profit; more debt
pushes it down directly; and the plug that absorbs the difference gets both pushes, which cancel.**
⇒ 🛑 **AND HERE IS THE PART THE WORD *"TAX"* HIDES, BECAUSE AN S CORPORATION PAYS NONE.** **The column above
headed *"the company's TAXABLE INCOME"* IS the shareholder's `K-1 box 1` — every dollar of it lands on OLEG's
personal 1040, not on a corporate bill.** ⇒ ⛔ **So Julia's ruling moves `K-1 box 1` by the WHOLE 20,872.61,
and it changes its SIGN:**

```
   MODEL A   page 1 line 22 = (10,294) − 1,033.21 interest        = (11,327)   ← a LOSS to him
   MODEL B   page 1 line 22 = (10,294) + 19,839.40 less insurance =   9,545    ← INCOME to him
                                                                   ----------
   the gap                                                           20,872.61
```

✅ **WHAT DOES NOT MOVE IS `box 16d`, the DISTRIBUTIONS — 132,583 on Model A against 132,582.40 on Model B,
the sixty cents being rounding.** 🔑 **So the honest sentence is: her ruling leaves his DISTRIBUTIONS alone
and swings his SHARE OF THE PROFIT from an 11,327 loss to 9,545 of income.** ⚠️ **That matters beyond this
return — §8 of this paper is the handoff to his 1040, and the two models hand it opposite numbers.**
⚠️ **An earlier version of this paper said the opposite on both limbs — it compared Model A against the

## 8 · 🔗 What flows to ANOTHER return — the handoff

⛔ **Not prepared, and not to be prepared from this paper.** The shareholder's 1040 is a separate
request on a separate day *(the one-return-per-request rule)*.

### 8A · The tables to carry across
**Pending** — the K-1 cannot be built until §6's first four items close.

### 8B · 🔴 What this side CANNOT supply
- **The shareholder's opening stock basis** — his 2024 **Form 7203 line 15**, filed with his 1040.
  ⚠️ **The firm may not hold it**; if not, it must be **reconstructed as separate scoped work.**
- **Whether 2024's 113,157 distribution exceeded his basis** and produced a capital gain he has
  already reported, or not.

### 8C · What must MATCH on both returns
- The **distribution** figure, and its presentation.
- Any **officer compensation** — his W-2 if one is issued.
- **The home-office treatment**: rent to the shareholder is **income on his 1040**.

### 8D · Before the other return is TRANSMITTED
- This return **filed and accepted**, and every §6 item closed.
